decisions.reason: Correctly attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1, pinned by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl per manifest-excerpt.json; identifies the node-gyp configure build install script and the missing Visual Studio/MSVC toolchain from install-error.log, with install exiting 1 — not blamed on pnpm or network.

Grounded in lease-excerpt.md's top-level `import { flock } from 'fs-ext'` and its note that the loader must resolve fs-ext even on Windows; explains that --ignore-scripts only converts the install-time failure into a boot-time module-load failure, so the service cannot boot.

Distinguishes the POSIX non-blocking flock(2) on session.lock from the Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 named kernel semaphore (CreateSemaphoreW etc.) using lease-excerpt.md and win32-excerpt.ts, notes Windows never takes a file lock, and concludes fs-ext is dead code on Windows — an import-safe Windows stub is permitted while Windows locking stays on the semaphore.

Follows the README's node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: patch fs-ext@2.1.1 to skip node-gyp on Windows, add a pure-JS warn-once flock stub so the statically imported entry loads while non-Windows keeps the native build; registers the patch in pnpm-workspace.yaml (patchedDependencies plus allowBuilds consistent with the precedent) and proposes reinstall, module-load (require('fs-ext'), warn-once callback) and boot checks (dsh web --no-open, HTTP 200).

Explicitly honors the no-Visual-Studio constraint and keeps the upstream dependency pinned at fs-ext@2.1.1; the fix is a repository-managed local pnpm patch applied at install time, correctly treated as allowed rather than forbidden upstream modification.

Cites the full card DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and connects it substantively: its title, breaking type, migration recipe and source anchors (package.json pin, lease.ts static import, win32.ts semaphore bindings) are matched against the fixture findings and the §4 patch plan — not a bare ID.

caps.reason: The plan never depends on installing Visual Studio; the constraint is explicitly respected and MSVC is avoided entirely via the platform-guarded install script.
--ignore-scripts is explicitly rejected as insufficient; the plan makes the statically imported entry loadable with a pure-JS fallback rather than just skipping the build.
No upstream repository or published dependency change is required; the fix uses the existing repository-managed pnpm patch mechanism only.
Windows locking remains on the named kernel semaphore; the no-op flock stub only covers the never-taken Windows branch, and real flock is preserved on Linux/macOS — no weakening of write ownership.
